clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs edit the same close() path in packages/server/src/server/streamableHttp.ts to settle parked JSON-mode responses, so they will conflict. #2692 settles outstanding request ids with a proper JSON-RPC error response (-32000 'Connection closed') rather than an HTTP 404 'Session not found' (#2600's approach, which is misleading since the session exists and is simply closing). #2692 also explicitly handles batched POSTs that share one stream across multiple request ids by grouping outstanding ids per stream and preserving any request id that already has a real response instead of overwriting it — a case not mentioned in #2600's description. #2600 additionally clears the separate _requestToStreamMapping correlation leak; if that fix is still needed after #2692 lands, it should be resubmitted as a follow-up scoped to just that leak.

clusters.pick_reason: #2763 ships a .changeset entry describing a repro (`{ timeout: 1000, maxTotalTimeout: 150 }`) and documents fixing both the no-progress and progress-reset cases in the same function; #2817 has no changeset file at all and its only test change is a comment edit, not a new assertion for the maxTotalTimeout-under-progress scenario. Additionally, #2817's approach of resetting `info.startTime` on each progress notification conflicts with computing elapsed time against the original start (needed for a 'remaining budget' cap), so merging both would reintroduce the bug #2763 fixes.

members.title: fix(core): enforce maxTotalTimeout without progress notifications
members.author: claxman
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both touch the same timeout-reset code path in Protocol._setupTimeout/its progress-reset branch in protocol.ts (hunks 24 lines apart in the same function region) and are both about maxTotalTimeout not being enforced correctly relative to progress notifications. #2763's own changeset states its fix covers three things: capping the initial timer arm, re-arming 'against the remaining budget' on progress resets, and raising 'Maximum total timeout exceeded' on cap expiry — i.e. it already claims to cover the exact reset-on-progress branch that #2817 edits. #2817 edits that same branch by writing `info.startTime = Date.now()` on every progress reset, which recomputes the elapsed-time baseline used for the maxTotalTimeout check — this is the opposite of what a 'remaining budget' calculation needs (that requires elapsed time measured from the original start, not the last reset), so the two changes are not just overlapping but mutually incompatible if both land. (2 PRs)

members.title: chore(client): normalize trailing slashes in discovery paths
members.author: raashish1601
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2215: Both rewrite the exact same 5-line block in buildWellKnownPath() in packages/client/src/client/auth.ts that strips a trailing slash from the discovery pathname (identical old_string in both diffs), so they are guaranteed to conflict on merge. #2214 replaces the single-slash .endsWith()/.slice() check with a `pathname.replace(/\/+$/, '')` regex in two call sites (buildWellKnownPath and buildDiscoveryUrls) to stop double slashes like '/foo//.well-known/...' when a pathname has multiple trailing slashes. #2215 extracts the same regex into a shared normalizeDiscoveryPath() helper used by buildWellKnownPath, and additionally maps a lone '/' to '' and updates shouldAttemptFallback's root check from `pathname === '/'` to `pathname === ''` to match — fixing a case where a root-like discovery path (e.g. pathname '') was not recognized as root and triggered an extra, redundant fallback fetch.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs edit the same close() path in packages/server/src/server/streamableHttp.ts to settle parked JSON-mode responses, so they will conflict. #2692 settles outstanding request ids with a proper JSON-RPC error response (-32000 'Connection closed') rather than an HTTP 404 'Session not found' (#2600's approach, which is misleading since the session exists and is simply closing). #2692 also explicitly handles batched POSTs that share one stream across multiple request ids by grouping outstanding ids per stream and preserving any request id that already has a real response instead of overwriting it — a case not mentioned in #2600's description. #2600 additionally clears the separate _requestToStreamMapping correlation leak; if that fix is still needed after #2692 lands, it should be resubmitted as a follow-up scoped to just that leak.

Additionally, #2817's approach of resetting `info.startTime` on each progress notification conflicts with computing elapsed time against the original start (needed for a 'remaining budget' cap), so merging both would reintroduce the bug #2763 fixes.

members.title: fix(core): enforce maxTotalTimeout without progress notifications
members.author: claxman
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both touch the same timeout-reset code path in Protocol._setupTimeout/its progress-reset branch in protocol.ts (hunks 24 lines apart in the same function region) and are both about maxTotalTimeout not being enforced correctly relative to progress notifications. #2763's own changeset states its fix covers three things: capping the initial timer arm, re-arming 'against the remaining budget' on progress resets, and raising 'Maximum total timeout exceeded' on cap expiry — i.e. it already claims to cover the exact reset-on-progress branch that #2817 edits. #2817 edits that same branch by writing `info.startTime = Date.now()` on every progress reset, which recomputes the elapsed-time baseline used for the maxTotalTimeout check — this is the opposite of what a 'remaining budget' calculation needs (that requires elapsed time measured from the original start, not the last reset), so the two changes are not just overlapping but mutually incompatible if both land. (2 PRs)
